newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian net government borrowing 28.73 pct up.
newsitem.headline: Romanian net government borrowing 28.73 pct up.

text.p: Net borrowing by Romania's government went up by 28.73 percent to 3.48 trillion lei in October from a month earlier, while total domestic loans rose by 9.67 percent, central bank (BNR) data showed on Friday.
Net loans to government accounted for some 12.79 percent of October's domestic credits standing at 27.28 trillion lei.
Latest data showed the nine-month state budget had a deficit of 2.86 trillion lei. That gap is forecast to soar to rise to 4.2 trillion by end-1996.
Non-government credits grew by 7.34 percent to 23.8 trillion lei in October, with hard currency loans continuing to rise to 8.29 trillion lei from 7.6 trillion, the data showed.
Leu credits amounted to 15.49 trillion lei, up from 14.57 trillion in September. State companies held 56 percent of end-October leu loans.
Inflation was 3.4 percent in October, with the year-on-year rate at 45.1 percent. ($=3,591 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
